issues.description: Animal member visibility is inconsistent between specification and solution: the UML and text require Animal(String), getName(), and setName(String) to be protected (UML shows "#" and the note explicitly says protected getter/setter), but the solution implements all three as public in Animal.java. This can confuse students about the required encapsulation and can break tests that enforce the specified access modifiers.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent: either change Animal.java so Animal(String), getName(), and setName(String) are protected (keeping name private), or update the UML and the note in the problem statement to require public visibility.

issues.description: Farm getter/setter requirement in the problem statement is not reflected in the UML: the text says to "implement a getter and a setter" for the farm's animals list, but the UML for Farm only lists animals, addAnimal, singFarmSongVerse, singFarmSong, and feedAllAnimals (no getAnimals/setAnimals). This mismatch leaves students unsure whether getAnimals()/setAnimals() are required and whether they are part of the graded API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align spec and UML: either add getAnimals(): List<Animal> and setAnimals(List<Animal>): void (with intended visibility) to the UML, or remove the getter/setter requirement from the problem statement if they are not intended to be implemented/tested.
